subject: OptiStore trial kickoff — ownership, success metrics & buyflow next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jensen <sam.jensen@optistore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Mar 2028 19:12:00 +0000
Subject: OptiStore trial kickoff — ownership, success metrics & buyflow next steps

Sam — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before the POC kickoff: 

High-level objective:
- Validate Redwood inference latency and cost targets for OptiStore's customer search reranking pipeline with 99%ile token latency <= 120ms and <= $0.0009/token in the steady-state workload.

Success criteria (agreed):
- Integration: production-like API connectivity + prefix caching enabled for at least 2 search endpoints.
- Performance: 99th percentile inference latency under 120ms for 512-token requests across 3 regions (US primary + two failover zones).
- Economics: per-token cost within the target above during a 48-hour soak at projected QPS.
- Security: SOC2 evidence and KMS integration validated for PII-bearing requests.

Proposed evaluation plan and timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): sign SOW / PO, agree on infra access (VPC peering or dedicated pool).
- Week 1: Redwood engineers provision a dedicated test pool; OptiStore engineers run sample traffic and smoke tests.
- Week 2: soak run (48 hours) and quality checks against your golden prompt set.
- Week 3: readout + handoff to production plan (if metrics met).

Ownership snapshot (RACI-lite):
- OptiStore infra (networking & VPC peering): Responsible = OptiStore (Priya / infra team), Consulted = Redwood infra eng (Karthik).
- App integration (API keys, route testing): Responsible = OptiStore app team (Sam), Accountable = Alex (Redwood AM).
- Security/compliance (SOC2 evidence, KMS): Responsible = OptiStore security (Priya), Support = Redwood security (Monica).
- Procurement/SOW: Responsible = OptiStore procurement (VP procurement), Accountable = OptiStore legal & Alex for Redwood pricing alignment.

Attachments: attached a short POC playbook with checklist and the draft SOW template (redwood-poc-playbook.pdf).

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm procurement cadence and whether a PO or DocuSign SOW is preferred?
2) Please share the contact for network/VPC setup and any required firewall IP allowlists.
3) We propose kickoff on Thursday — I sent a tentative calendar invite (will update after procurement confirmation).

If that looks right, I'll loop in our infra lead (Karthik) to start the VPC peering options and Monica for the SOC2 artifacts.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-poc-playbook.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

From: Sam Jensen <sam.jensen@optistore.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@optistore.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OptiStore trial kickoff — ownership, success metrics & buyflow next steps

Thanks Alex — this is helpful and aligns with our internal view. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement: our procurement team prefers a DocuSign SOW + PO combo. VP procurement will sign the PO, but legal wants the SOW in DocuSign first.
- Network contact: Priya (Cc) will own the VPC peering work — she will share an engineer and IP allowlist by EOD Friday.
- Security: Priya will coordinate our CISO's checklist; they'll need the SOC2 report and a short whitepaper on KMS integration flow.

I attached our internal POC scope summary to help align the load pattern and sample prompts (optistore-poc-scope.pdf).

Couple of asks from our execs: could Redwood provide a brief one-pager on fallback behavior and graceful degradation for regional outages? They'll want to see how you maintain latency SLAs under partial outage.

We can do kickoff Thursday at 14:00 PT; I'll accept the invite once procurement confirms.

—Sam
Sam Jensen
Senior Product Manager, Search
OptiStore
Attachment: optistore-poc-scope.pdf (PDF, 24KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Sam Jensen <sam.jensen@optistore.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: OptiStore trial kickoff — ownership, success metrics & buyflow next steps

Thanks for the context. A few operational clarifications from the infra side and a concrete ownership table we can operate against during the POC: 

Operational notes:
- VPC peering or Private Deployment: we can support either. For a fast turnaround I'd recommend Dedicated (reserved test pool) with an IP allowlist. VPC peering is fine but often adds network ops lead time.
- Allowlist: we'll provide a minimal set of egress IPs and a short NAT/route guide.
- Soak traffic: please include a steady-state profile + a 10m burst test to validate tail-latency behavior.

Proposed ownership (final RACI entries):
- Networking/VPC peering: R: OptiStore (Priya's engineer), A: OptiStore infra lead, C: Redwood infra (Karthik), I: Redwood AM (Alex).
- Test harness & traffic generation: R: OptiStore devops, A: OptiStore product (Sam), C: Redwood SRE (Monica), I: Karthik.
- Model/config rollouts (quantization profile, batching): R: Redwood infra eng, A: Redwood infra eng, C: OptiStore ML lead, I: Alex.
- Security evidence (SOC2, KMS flow): R: Redwood security (Monica) for supplying artifacts, A: OptiStore security for acceptance.

Procurement path suggestion (buyflow):
1) DocuSign SOW (technical scope + success metrics) —> 2) OptiStore legal review (1–3 business days) —> 3) PO issuance by procurement —> 4) Redwood signs and provisions test pool.

I'll prepare a short network checklist for Priya and a minimal IP allowlist this afternoon. Alex — happy to join the kickoff to walk through the test harness and the rollback/fallback behavior Sam asked for.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: optistore-network-checklist.txt (plain text, 3KB)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jensen <sam.jensen@optistore.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@optistore.com>

Subject: Re: OptiStore trial kickoff — ownership, success metrics & buyflow next steps

Great — thanks everyone for the quick turn. Agreed on the DocuSign path. Action summary and owners: 

ACTIONS (owners + target dates):
- Alex: Share DocuSign SOW draft (redwood -> OptiStore) by EOD today. Link: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123DEF
- Priya: Share VPC contact + allowlist (by 2028-03-16 end of day).
- Karthik: Send minimal IP allowlist and network checklist (by 2028-03-14 EOD) — noted attached.
- Monica: Package SOC2 artifacts + KMS integration notes (by 2028-03-17).
- Sam: Confirm PO cadence and approve kickoff time once procurement confirms (target: 2028-03-15).

Kickoff: Tentative calendar invite at Thu 14:00 PT — I'll finalize once we have procurement path confirmed.

Readout expectations: we'll run the soak during Week 2 and schedule a results readout the next business day. If any metric is missed we'll capture root cause and provide a remediation plan — typical remediation lanes include small batching changes, prefix cache tuning, or failover routing to a warmer model variant.

Attachments referenced in this thread: redwood-poc-playbook.pdf, optistore-poc-scope.pdf, optistore-sow-draft.docx

I'll drop a one-pager on graceful degradation (regional fallback + degraded feature set) into the kickoff deck before the meeting. Thanks — talk soon.
